Grant purpose as a tiebreak signal

Source: R/purpose.R
pf_purpose.Rd

Part XIV column (d), SIGOCPYPOGOC, asks the filer what the grant was for. This module turns that free text into a comparison against the recipient's own self-description and uses it to break ties the name cascade could not.

Why a tiebreak and not a score

Measured on 63 adjudicated MAYBE grants and 794 YES grants (dev/PURPOSE-MATCH-FINDINGS.md):

  • The purpose is contentless 58.9% of the time (median 2 words), and when it has content the comparison still separates candidates on only half of grants. It is silent far more often than it is wrong.

  • Added to the linkage score across all pairs it is a net loss on grants that were already right (−14 of 794 at w = 0.4), and it would shift the score distribution the YES/MAYBE/NO thresholds are tuned against.

  • Confined to the tie band it gains without losing, and the weight stops mattering — which is the signature of a tiebreak rather than a score term. So it is implemented as one, and the weight disappears.

The measured gain is small and rests on few cases: +1 grant of 61 at npmatch's own gates, +3 if the tie_high gate is dropped. It is therefore off by default; see pf_purpose_tiebreak().
